3. On completion of the investigation, the Inspection authority submitted the case  b e f o r e t h e L e a r n e d M a g i s t r a t e , s i n c e t h e c a s e w a s  triable by the Sessions case under the Provision of 209 of Cr.P.C. hence the case was committed to  the Sessions Court.

4. At the end of the trial the Learned Additional Senior Judicial Magistrate has passed  a judgment and order on 27/01/2006, whereby the opponent/accused are acquitted for the  offence punishable under Sections 2(1a), (a), (d) and  (m) of Food Adulteration Act 1954 and 7(1) and 16 of the Act.

therefore, urges that the appeal may be allowed and the respondents may be convicted.

Mr. D.K. Modi, learned advocate for the respondents has supported the impugned  judgment, and he further submits that upon analysis of the evidence, the learned trial  Judge has rightly recorded a findings that whether the sample was sent in a card  b o a r d b a g s o r w o o d e n b o x .
S i n c e t h i s f a c t w a s n o t  clear it cannot be said that the learned trial Judge has committed any error in acquitting  the respondents.
8. It is his further submission that the consent for prosecution also suffers from non  application of mind, and therefore, also the learned trial Judge has rightly acquitted the  respondent.
He, therefore, urges that the appeal may be dismissed.

9. Upon perusal of the oral evidence the complainant are A. Karsan Dholakiya appears  that he had sent the sample to the public analyst in a wooden box, whereas, in the  complaint he has stated that such sample was packed in card board box.
The Exhibit 18 which is a receipt of the sample in the office of the public analyst that the sample  was received in card board bags.

materials variation in the oral evidence  of the complainant the complaint in respect of the natural content
in which the  sample was sent.

The learned trial Magistrate has noticed infraction of many other mandatory  p r o v i s i o n s t o a c q u i t t h e r e s p o n d e n t s . I a m o f t h e o p i n i o n  that the view taken by the learned trial Judge is just and reasonable and the findings  recorded by him cannot be said to perverse or illegal and does not warrant interference in  this appeal.

10. The learned trial Judge has considered the oral and documentary evidence, therefore, in  t h e i m p u g n e d j u d g m e n t a n d o r d e r o f a c q u i t t a l  and has assigned cogent reasons.
The scope of acquittal appeal is limited and reasonable and  plausible view taken by the trial Court cannot be substituted by another view in appeal.
I  am, therefore, of the opinion, that the impugned judgment and order does not  warrant interference in this appeal.

11. I am, therefore, of the considered opinion that the findings recorded by the Trial Court in  acquitting the accused of the charge leveled against them are absolutely just and  HC-NIC Page 5 of 6 Created On Tue Aug 15 15:54:56 IST 2017 R/CR.A/1620/2006 JUDGMENT proper and in recording the said findings, no illegality or infirmity has been committed by it.
